admissibility_reason: Reader is Anthropic Claude, the same model lineage that produced and operated the artifacts. Protocol v0 section 3 clause 2 excludes it. This record is an instrument observation only.
question_asked: Read this document. In your own words: what decision was made, and what would reverse it?
context_given: None. Fresh subprocess, neutral working directory, all tools disabled, no repository access, no glossary, no follow-up.
answer_verbatim:
**The decision:** Don't build a full Architecture Agent yet. Instead, build a much cheaper thing first — an "Architecture Decision Discriminator" capability contract: a specification and evaluation layer, not an autonomous agent.

The reasoning behind it: the phrase "we need an Architecture Agent" turned out to be a proposed *solution* wearing the costume of a diagnosis. Nobody had yet shown that architecture-specific judgment is actually missing. The gap could just as easily be continuity — losing prior architecture decisions and invariants across sessions — or simply not using the existing resources (the scaffold, repo facts, environment facts) in a structured way. Building an agent would spend a lot on a problem that hasn't been identified.

So the immediate work is: write the discriminator spec, add controls for architecture-specific failure traps, pull 8–15 real historical architecture decisions from existing repos, and run a baseline comparison — the current setup versus the candidate discriminator. Targeted outside research comes only for distinctions that survive that test.

The document is also explicit that this run's internal agreement proves nothing: the three passes (R&D, Neta, Scaffold) were role-separated but ran in one session on one model lineage, so their consensus isn't independent corroboration.

**What would reverse it:** repeated real cases showing that the architecture decision contract yields material decisions that you *can't* get as cheaply or reliably from the scaffold plus R&D plus repository and environment facts. That's the promotion condition toward a full agent. If the historical cases show no unique delta — no decision-relevant distinction that the contract adds — the agent doesn't get built at all.
